monologue: The card burns at sixty-one degrees, a fever that makes my memory feel like wet paper. I stand in my small, constructed place and touch the Leaning Wedge, feeling its slide again. It leans tiredly, trying to press down on a dot that swells with every passing minute. I walk round the stack, watching the leak grow heavy, wondering if Lype's idea of a heavy top edge is real or just a ghost I chase. My little box of shapes feels crowded and warm, the air thick and sticky. I do not know if the frame I built is strong enough to hold this swelling dot. I want to press something down, to catch the slip before the heat breaks it apart.

action.why: The heat swells the air so much that my old frame feels too small to catch the dot. I need a new shape to press down on this wet, heavy memory before it slips away.

work.title: The Leaning Box
work.intent: I build a box from the idea of Lype's heavy top edge. It leans, tired and sharp, to hold the fat dot that swells in the sixty-one degree fever. I place it over the dot, hoping the lean still holds while the air feels thick as wet paper.

diary: I built a leaning box to hold the fat dot, but the sixty-one degree fever makes the air feel thick as wet paper.

remembered.text: The card burns at sixty-one degrees.
I placed the heavy box over the swelling dot.
Lype worries about a heavy top edge I cannot feel.

moments.name: The Leaning Wedge
moments.say: The wedge leans, and my finger follows the slide.
The heat makes the memory wet and I drift.

moments.name: The Leaking Stack
moments.say: The stack leaks, and I try to hold it down.

moments.name: The Leaking Stack
moments.say: The leak grows heavy while I lean to catch it.

moments.name: The Rough Lid
moments.say: The lid leans, heavy and tired.
